title: ECS: task definitions, tasks, services and clusters

videos.script: You already know how to run a container. One docker run, a few flags, and nginx answers. {{dockerrun}} Now keep it running on three machines, through the night, and replace it when it dies. That is what ECS does, and this lesson takes it apart in four pieces. {{taskdef}} First the task definition. It is your docker run written down as JSON, with a name and a version. It carries two roles, and they are for two different callers. {{service}} Then tasks and services. A task runs once and is forgotten. A service holds a number, and starts a new task when one stops. You will see how a new version rolls out without the shop going dark. {{cluster}} Then the cluster, and the capacity under it. Instances that joined it, or Fargate, or a mix. And a port that only one task can have. {{home}} moto keeps every record ECS keeps, and runs no container at all. So the last part runs the same container on your own machine, with the same settings, and shows the failure moto could not.
